reasons.C: Closest movement and stance: opens on a reflective question, long semicolon-chained sentences, 'it seems to me', and a closing 'Perhaps...not X but Y' turn like the passage; the brief second-person aside is the one slip.
reasons.A: Long, clause-heavy sentences with semicolon series and measured hedging ('arguably', 'curiously') fit well, but the closing rhetorical question plus 'I suspect' ends more chattily than the passage's quiet summation.
reasons.B: Right register and hedges, but the sentences are shorter and more segmented (separate 'It comes... It names... And...' sentences), with less of the passage's long, balanced periodic flow.
reasons.D: Plain, punchy, second-person advice-column voice with short sentences, enumerated 'First/Second/Third', contractions and quoted dialogue; nothing like the passage's reflective, long-sentenced 'we'.
